name: Abasi 5% EC Insecticide and Miticide
sizes: 50 ml, 100 ml, 250 ml, 500 ml and 1 Litre
uses: thrips, spider mites, leaf miners and aphids
targets: Thrips and spider mites on roses (nematodes as a dip); mites and caterpillars on tomatoes; leaf miners and aphids on cucumbers and French beans
lead: Abasi 5% EC is an abamectin insecticide and miticide for growers of roses and vegetables. It controls thrips and spider mites, can be used as a dip against nematodes on roses, and protects tomatoes, cucumbers and French beans from mites, caterpillars, leaf miners and aphids.
dose: Application rate 200 to 300 ml per hectare in 1000 litres of water.
method: Half-fill the spray tank with water, add the required amount of Abasi 5EC, top up to the level and agitate until uniform. Spray immediately after mixing, covering both leaf surfaces.
extraSteps: Abamectin acts by contact and stomach action with translaminar movement, so treated pests stop feeding soon after contact.
Rotate with insecticides from other chemical groups.

name: Agro-Lambda 5EC Insecticide
uses: aphids and thrips on tomatoes and vegetables
targets: Aphids and thrips on tomatoes and other vegetables
settings: Agricultural: vegetable growers, small and medium plots and kitchen gardens
lead: Agro-Lambda 5EC is a lambda-cyhalothrin insecticide for control of aphids and thrips on tomatoes and other vegetables. Both pests weaken plants, spoil fruit quality and can spread disease if left unchecked.
method: Mix as the label directs and spray in the early morning or late afternoon, avoiding windy or rainy conditions. Cover the underside of leaves and inside flowers, where pests hide.
extraSteps: Scout regularly and start protection when you first see pests, rather than waiting for heavy damage.
Pyrethroids are harmful to bees and fish: do not spray open flowers where bees are working and keep spray and rinse water away from streams, ponds and fish.
Rotate with insecticides from different chemical groups to slow resistance.

name: ALONZE 50EC Abamectin Insecticide
sizes: 25 ml, 50 ml, 100 ml, 250 ml and 1 Litre
uses: spider mites, thrips, leaf miners and nematodes
targets: Spider mites in roses and carnations; thrips and leaf miners in vegetables; nematodes in potatoes
lead: ALONZE 50EC is an abamectin insecticide, miticide and nematicide with contact and translaminar action. It controls spider mites, thrips and leaf miners on flowers and vegetables, and nematodes in potatoes.
dose: Foliar spray: 0.15 L per hectare in 1000 L of water (3 ml per 20 L). Potato nematodes: soil drench of 240 to 300 ml per hectare in 1000 L of water.
preHarvest: chilies, broccoli and snow peas 7 days; runner beans, tomatoes and French beans 3 days; potatoes 14 days. Do not harvest before the interval has passed.
method: Half-fill the tank with clean water, add the measured product, top up and agitate. Spray in calm weather with good coverage of leaf undersides, where mites and thrips hide.
extraSteps: Apply at the first signs of pests, repeat after 7 days, and do not exceed 3 applications.
Rotate with products from other groups and keep spray away from streams, ponds and fish.

name: Amito 5.7WDG Insecticide
uses: fall armyworm and caterpillars on vegetables and field crops
targets: Fall armyworm, caterpillars and other chewing pests
settings: Agricultural: vegetable farms and field crops such as maize
lead: Amito 5.7WDG is an emamectin benzoate insecticide in water-dispersible granule form for fall armyworm, caterpillars and other chewing pests on vegetables and field crops. Act early, while larvae are small, to protect your yield.
method: Weigh or measure the granules and stir them into water in the spray tank, then apply as a spray. On maize direct the spray into the whorl; on vegetables cover both sides of the leaves.
extraSteps: Scout fields regularly, look for fresh feeding damage and frass, and spray when pests are first seen.
Rotate with products from other chemical groups and keep to the number of applications allowed on the label.

name: Ampligo 150ZC Insecticide
uses: fall armyworm, bollworm, diamondback moth, thrips and aphids
targets: Caterpillars (fall armyworm, bollworm, diamondback moth, cutworms) and sucking pests (thrips, aphids, whiteflies)
settings: Agricultural: vegetable and field crop farms
lead: Syngenta Ampligo 150ZC is a dual-action insecticide that combines chlorantraniliprole and lambda-cyhalothrin. It controls fall armyworm, bollworm, diamondback moth, cutworms, thrips, aphids and whiteflies, and is classified WHO Class II.
method: Mix as the label directs and spray in calm weather, early morning or late afternoon, making sure the spray reaches where pests feed.
extraSteps: Scout regularly and begin spraying when pests first appear, because small larvae are easier to control.
Lambda-cyhalothrin is harmful to bees and fish: do not spray open flowers where bees are active and keep spray and rinse water out of streams and ponds.

name: Bazooka 18EC Insecticide
uses: spider mites and leaf miners on French beans and tomatoes
targets: Spider mites and leaf miners on French beans, tomatoes and other crops
settings: Agricultural: French bean and tomato growers and other crops
lead: Greenlife Bazooka 18EC is a broad-spectrum miticide and insecticide containing abamectin 18 g/L. It controls spider mites and leaf miners on French beans, tomatoes and other crops, where mites multiply fastest in hot, dry weather.
method: Half-fill the tank with water, add the measured product, top up and agitate. Spray in calm weather, early morning or late afternoon, with good coverage on both sides of the leaf.
extraSteps: Scout regularly, checking the underside of leaves for mites and mines, and start spraying when pests first show up.
Rotate with products from other chemical groups and keep to the number of sprays on the label, because mites can become resistant quickly.

name: Engeo 247SC
uses: pests on vegetables, fruits and other crops
targets: A wide range of crop pests (pest list to be confirmed on the label)
settings: Agricultural: vegetables, fruits and other crops
lead: Engeo 247SC is an insecticide for crop protection that controls a wide range of pests. It suits vegetables, fruits and other crops and supports healthy plant growth.
method: Mix and apply exactly as the manufacturer's label directs, shaking the container well and agitating the tank while you spray. Never mix with other products unless the label allows it.

name: Indoking 300SC Insecticide
uses: bollworms, caterpillars and leaf miners on roses
targets: Bollworms, caterpillars and leaf miners on roses and other crops
settings: Agricultural and floriculture: rose farms, vegetables and field crops
lead: Greenlife Indoking 300SC is an indoxacarb insecticide for control of bollworms, caterpillars and leaf miners on roses and other crops. Early control of chewing pests protects buds, flowers and leaves from damage that can make flowers unsellable.
method: Shake the container well, half-fill the tank with water, add the measured product, top up and agitate throughout. Spray evenly and thoroughly in calm weather, early morning or late afternoon.
extraSteps: Scout regularly, checking buds, shoots and the underside of leaves, and start spraying when pests first appear.
Rotate with insecticides from other chemical groups, keep to the number of applications on the label, and avoid spraying where bees are active.

name: Kingcode Elite 50EC Insecticide
uses: thrips, aphids and whiteflies on roses and vegetables
targets: Thrips, aphids and whiteflies on roses, French beans, kales, tomatoes and other crops
settings: Agricultural: rose, French bean, kale and tomato growers
lead: Greenlife Kingcode Elite 50EC combines lambda-cyhalothrin and acetamiprid in a broad-spectrum insecticide for thrips, aphids and whiteflies. It protects roses, French beans, kales, tomatoes and other crops from pests that multiply quickly in warm weather.
method: Half-fill the tank with water, add the measured product, top up and agitate. Spray evenly in calm weather, early morning or late afternoon, covering the underside of leaves where whiteflies and aphids hide.
extraSteps: Scout crops regularly and start spraying when pests first appear.
Both active ingredients can harm bees and aquatic life: avoid spraying open flowers where bees are active and keep spray and rinse water out of streams and ponds.

name: Pegasus 500SC Insecticide
uses: mites, whiteflies and diamondback moth on cabbage and kale
targets: Mites, whiteflies and diamondback moth on cabbage, kale and other vegetables
settings: Agricultural: commercial and small vegetable farms
lead: Pegasus 500SC is a diafenthiuron insecticide and acaricide that controls mites, whiteflies and diamondback moth on cabbage, kale and other vegetables. It gives vegetable growers a different active ingredient to rotate against pests that are hard to control.
method: Mix as the label directs and spray in the early morning or late afternoon, making sure the spray reaches the underside of leaves where whiteflies and mites hide.
extraSteps: Scout fields at least weekly and spray when pests reach damaging levels rather than on a fixed calendar alone.
Rotate insecticides with different modes of action, use clean seedlings and remove crop residues after harvest.
